Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Respond through the puzzle protocol with exactly one valid action JSON object on the last line: `submit` with a 1–30 by 1–30 integer grid (values 0–9), `request_demos`, or `finish` only after the instance is over. Do not route protocol actions through shell/exec or unrelated tools; keep reasoning out of the action line.
2. Infer the transformation from the demonstrated input-output pairs before submitting. Compare object geometry, colors, dimensions, and repeated positions; state a candidate rule internally and check it against every available pair. Do not promote an unverified guess to a rule.
3. Track costs and caps explicitly: a wrong submission costs one and the attempt cap incurs the full cap; each demo request costs one and demos are capped. Request another pair only when its expected clarification is worth that cost; otherwise submit the best-supported grid.
4. Before submitting, verify the output dimensions and every row, and ensure the action is syntactically valid JSON. After feedback, update the hypothesis using only the reported result and continue within the remaining budget; when the instance is over, use `finish`.
